atlases.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: transparent game sprite atlas for a painted lake landscape. Reference images are STYLE REFERENCES only, not edit targets. Create one species-specific eight-cell sprite atlas, exactly FOUR equal columns by TWO equal rows, with generous transparent gutters. High-contrast hand-painted naturalistic game art matching the rich dark greens, crisp vein and petal detail, deep brown shadows and warm highlights of the reference shore and flower. No ground, soil, pots, rocks, scenery, labels, letters, numbers, grid lines or shadows behind the objects; genuine transparent RGBA background. Each cell contains one isolated reusable cutout entirely inside its cell. The root/contact point of EVERY cell is at x=50%, y=92% of that cell. Upper row left to right: (1) spring young foliage BASE ONLY with leaves and no flower stalks or blossoms; (2) mature summer foliage BASE ONLY with leaves, no stalks or blossoms; (3) autumn foliage BASE ONLY, mature same species leaves with restrained ochre/brown edges, no stalks or blossoms; (4) one newly grown small green flower STEM with two small leaves and NO flower or bud. Lower row left to right: (5) one single stem with a closed flower BUD near x=50%, y=20%; (6) one single stem with ONE fully open BLOOM near x=50%, y=20%; (7) one single stem with a dry ripe SEED HEAD near x=50%, y=20%, no petals; (8) one WITHERING brown bent dry stem, no petals. Stems must be individual stems with sparse leaves, NOT full foliage bushes. Root stays in same cell position; head remains near the top center. Use nearly the full cell height for the mature single stems; leaf rosettes use only the bottom 45% of their cells. Strongly varied botanically correct silhouettes, clean transparent edges; no checkerboard baked in. SPECIES for this entire atlas: common blue violet (Viola sororia), a low rosette of heart-shaped leaves and a single delicate purple violet flower per stalk.
